standard.title: Paraphrase and justify opinions
standard.description: Use appropriate interaction skills including paraphrasing and questioning to clarify meaning, make connections to own experience, and present and justify an opinion or idea
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can listen for key points and information and contribute to discussions by expressing opinions and making judgements (AC9E4LY02). They have not yet applied paraphrasing as a clarification strategy, or developed systematic approaches to questioning for meaning-making in discussion.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use paraphrasing and purposeful questioning to clarify meaning in discussions, make connections between what they hear and their own experience, and present and justify opinions with supporting reasons.

nodes.label: Paraphrasing to clarify
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can paraphrase what a speaker has said to check understanding and signal attention, and use this as a clarification strategy in discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: In a discussion context, paraphrase at least one contribution from another speaker to check understanding, and explain what paraphrasing does for the conversation.
nodes.typical_width: Use paraphrasing to check understanding and signal engagement across discussion contexts. Explain the difference between paraphrasing (capturing meaning in own words) and summarising (condensing) and echo (repeating). Apply paraphrasing as a strategy to keep conversations moving and build shared understanding.
wider: Practise paraphrasing in paired and group contexts with explicit feedback on accuracy — developing awareness of what is captured and what is lost in a paraphrase
Compare how paraphrasing functions differently in formal discussion versus informal conversation contexts — discussing when the strategy is most useful

response_modes.reason: Paraphrasing is a skill that requires practice to become automatic. Students often confuse paraphrasing with repeating or summarising. Consolidation through deliberate practice in structured discussion contexts builds reliable deployment before paraphrasing is integrated with questioning and justification.

success_criteria: Paraphrases a speaker's contribution accurately — captures the meaning in own words without significantly distorting it.
Uses paraphrasing as a clarification strategy — checks understanding rather than just replaying what was said.

nodes.label: Purposeful questioning for meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can ask specific questions to clarify a speaker's meaning, and use questioning to move a discussion forward rather than just to gather information.
nodes.minimum_width: In a discussion, ask at least one specific clarifying question that targets a gap in understanding or an unstated assumption in what a speaker has said.
nodes.typical_width: Ask specific questions to clarify meaning, make constructive comments that keep conversation moving, and use questions to invite elaboration or probe assumptions. Apply a range of question types: clarifying, extending, probing, inviting connection.
wider: Explore how different question types serve different discussion purposes — comparing how clarifying questions, open questions, and devil's advocate questions function in building shared understanding
Examine question types across formal and informal discussion contexts and discuss how formality shapes which question types are appropriate
success_criteria: Asks a specific clarifying question that targets meaning — not a display question or a factual check.
The question is purposeful — it opens up discussion or clarifies understanding rather than closing conversation down.

nodes.label: Present and justify opinions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present an opinion clearly and support it with reasons, making connections to their own experience where relevant and choosing vocabulary suited to the context.
nodes.minimum_width: Present an opinion in a discussion context with at least two reasons supporting it, and respond to at least one contribution from another speaker in the discussion.
nodes.typical_width: Present and justify opinions across formal and informal discussion contexts, choosing vocabulary and sentence structures appropriate to purpose and formality. Make connections between their own contributions and those of others. Respond constructively to challenge or different perspectives.
wider: Participate in a structured debate or formal discussion, applying all interaction skills (paraphrasing, questioning, justifying) in an integrated performance and reflecting on what worked and what could be improved
Apply different registers — formal and informal — to presenting the same opinion in different contexts, and discuss how register choice affects persuasiveness and appropriateness

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to integrate paraphrasing (node 1), purposeful questioning (node 2), and opinion presentation into a coherent interactive performance — the full capability demand of the descriptor. Phase collapse here means students default to opinion-delivery without the interactive skills that make discussion productive.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of discussion contexts — pair, group, class, formal presentation, debate — and the range of communication purposes — clarifying, connecting, persuading, extending — provide genuine richness. Advancing students can develop flexible deployment of interaction skills across formal and informal contexts.
success_criteria: Presents an opinion with at least two supporting reasons in a discussion context.
Responds to at least one other speaker — through paraphrasing, questioning, or building on their point — demonstrating interaction rather than turn-taking.
